chapter: Pianists, the district and Stormy Weather
title: Cornet players D.D. and Billy and Blue's drinking
summary: Talk about a cornetist and his work with D.D. and Billy, then Blue's drinking, and the number of jobs in his book.

story.theme_name: Drink, drugs and the bandstand's casualties
story.community_name: Drugs and drink on the bandstand and the road

blocks.x: Is that fine? Yeah. What about your fellows you work with? Did any of them sing in French? Yeah. Well, they sing in a trio.

Yeah. Did they? I'm the one who got the d'eat. Yeah. I'm the one who got the d'eat. Where's that now? Really? Yeah. I told them I got a cornet player. I'd like to be all the young. His name, I forgot his name too.
He used to live right across the street from where I used to go around and go. You know? I was the one who got the d'eat. I was the one who got the d'eat. I was the one who got the d'eat.
I was the one who got the d'eat. I was the one who got the d'eat. I was the one who got the d'eat. I was the one who got the d'eat. Where's that now?

Yeah. I told them I got a cornet player. I'd like to be all the young. His name, I forgot his name too. He used to live right across the street from where I used to go around and go. You know, even the d'eat was there. I played with many jobs with the d'eat. He used to play around about four or four or two together. Yeah. With Billy.
He played down there a long time. I even got back here, coach. Yeah. Yeah.
Anyway, you played with the d'eat a lot, huh? Oh, man.
D.D. and Billy. Yes, indeed. He played with them a lot.
What about, you were saying about Manuel's son that played for that. Was he good? No. He was never as good as his dad. No. Couldn't play like his dad. He drank too much wine. Drunk all the time.

You can't do nothing drunk. He might have been. See, like Blue. Blue used to drink all the last. Blue was a good trumpet player. He could sing a whole lot, you know? He'd bring his wine. I'd bring wine for him. I'd buy him a bottle. He'd bring. But I wouldn't give it to him until he'd be knocking off. Yeah. Let him drink all he wanted. He'd get drunk with him. Just put him in the car and take him home. That's all. What he wasn't going to drink. Yeah, poor Blue. When I told him, I said, Blue, don't be drinking so much. He said, oh man, I know what I'm doing, I know what I'm doing. I know what I'm doing. He knew what he was doing. He used to send more to two eyes. I loved it, you know what I'm saying? And then he went, I don't know why we prayed and made them people. He used to make them steps, you know? He used to make them steps. I don't believe.
I don't believe, because he was kind of, his feet were bad or something.

I used to make them steps like a Japanese man. You know, they make them steps forward, backwards, make them dialect. And we played a great job. I got my book and all my jobs in there. I had four jobs in one month. I said, how many of you got this one? I said, I got four. Four? I said, yeah, I got four. Four. No less than two. Then my role was even bigger. I said, I'd rather make them trip to California. Then when she died down there, I said, no. I got all my people in California. I got a, my cousin out there, he's been out there 50 years. He must be 87 years old by now. He never wrote me a letter. Not one letter. Because his sister brought him out there on the pass to work in Fresno alone in the sawmill. She took a hundred dollars out there to work. And she stayed out. Of course, she's dead now. But he's living. And her husband is dead. I don't know what she's going to do.
